subject: Clarify: Non-learning guarantee, tombstone process, and TTL carveouts
messages:
From: Lisa Cohen <lisa.cohen@optimahealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: security@optimahealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Oct 2029 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Quick confirmation: 'no training' + log retention carveouts

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week — OptimaHealth is moving fast on the evaluation. Before we proceed to legal, our Security team asked for two short confirmations to include in the SOC questionnaire:

1) A plain-language assurance that Redwood does not use customer-provided production requests to update or train model weights ("no training on customer data").
2) A description of your tombstone/erase process and any TTL exceptions: e.g., are debug snapshots, traces, or KV-cache artifacts retained anywhere beyond the stated TTL; how are backup/archival copies handled?

We want this to be narrow and operational (not marketing). Would you be able to provide a short, authoritative paragraph and point to the internal runbook or artifact we can attach? Also flag any cases where logs are retained for longer because of debugging, legal hold, or platform telemetry.

Appreciate the quick turn here — security needs to include a snippet tomorrow.

Best,
Lisa
Director, Security Operations
OptimaHealth

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: 'no training' + log retention carveouts

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Drafting an operational response below; looping in Ben for customer context and Marissa for legal/wording.

Plain-language assurance (draft):
Redwood does not use customer production inputs to train or update model weights. Customer requests and responses are not incorporated into training datasets or used to modify model parameters. We may retain ephemeral runtime telemetry (for routing, caching, and debugging) for a limited TTL; those artifacts are isolated from any training pipelines and are subject to access controls described below.

Tombstone/erase process (draft summary):
- Erasure request: When a customer issues a data erase, we tombstone identifiers and expunge associated ephemeral caches and indexed artifacts within the configured erase window (default 30 days).
- Backups & snapshots: Full system backups are rotated and encrypted; backups older than retention TTL are destroyed via a scheduled secure-deletion job. Customers requiring accelerated destruction can request a manual purge for their slices, which we log and attest to.
- TTL exceptions: We do not retain customer content for training, but certain diagnostic artifacts (aggregate telemetry or anonymized sampling) may be kept for longer operational analysis unless the customer opts out. Legal holds or court orders can also temporarily suspend deletion for the affected account.

Runbook link (internal): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Erase-Runbook (public excerpt attached).

If this looks good, Marissa — any legal tweaks before I send a final paragraph they can drop into the questionnaire? Ben — any product caveats I should call out for OptimaHealth's regulated workflows?

Thanks,
Neha
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Oct 2029 07:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: 'no training' + log retention carveouts

Neha — thanks for the draft. A few suggested edits to keep this defensible for audits and to avoid absolute-sounding commitments:

1) Replace "does not use" with "does not use customer-provided production inputs to train or update model weights unless explicitly agreed in writing" — this covers managed research engagements and prevents accidental overpromise.
2) For "tombstone identifiers and expunge associated ephemeral caches" add a note about timelines: make the default erase window explicit (30 days) and call out that some replication or disaster-recovery copies may remain longer but are included in scheduled secure deletion.
3) For telemetry, recommend specifying examples (rate-limiting metrics, anonymized latency histograms) and state that these are aggregated and stripped of PII before any retention beyond TTL.

Proposed final paragraph (legal-friendly):
Redwood does not use customer-provided production inputs to train or update model weights unless an explicit written agreement states otherwise. Production requests and content are excluded from model training pipelines. Redwood may retain operational telemetry and encrypted system snapshots for debugging and continuity purposes under a documented TTL; any longer-term retention for operational analytics uses aggregated, non-identifiable data only. Deletion requests are processed per our erase runbook (default erase window: 30 days); replication or backup copies are subject to scheduled secure-deletion jobs unless affected by lawful hold.

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Hi Lisa — attaching a short, audit-ready paragraph your Security team can paste into the questionnaire (below). We kept it operational and intentionally conservative.

Final paragraph for questionnaire:
"Redwood does not use customer-provided production inputs to train or update model weights unless an explicit written agreement states otherwise. Production requests and content are excluded from our model training pipelines. Redwood may retain limited operational telemetry and encrypted system snapshots for debugging and continuity purposes under documented TTLs (default erase window: 30 days). Any longer-term analytics retention uses aggregated, non-identifiable data; replication and backup copies are removed via scheduled secure-deletion jobs except where retention is lawfully required (e.g., legal hold)."
